standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of ampleness by the basis of the topology given by the affine opens defined by homogeneous forms in the section ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 9427-9432 and again at proof lines 9483-9485
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite cover by affine opens cut out by homogeneous sections and, later, the global generation of all large powers.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of sections of a power of an invertible sheaf over a distinguished affine open as quotients of homogeneous sections, and the characterization of locally finite type morphisms by finite type ring maps on affine charts
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns generators of the coordinate rings of the affine opens into homogeneous sections of a single large power.

standard_prerequisites.name: The construction of a morphism to projective space from a generating set of sections of an invertible sheaf, and the identification of the pullback of the twisting sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the morphism j with the correct pullback of the twisting sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: Permanence of immersions under base change and products, the Segre embedding, and closedness of composites of immersions
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the morphism produced in the second half is again an immersion.

core_obligations: Choose a finite affine cover adapted to the base: using the ample characterization, the affine opens defined by homogeneous sections form a basis, so pick finitely many a_0 to a_n such that the corresponding opens cover X, are affine, and each maps into an affine open of S (proof lines 9427-9440).

Make the coordinate rings finitely generated by homogeneous sections: by the locally finite type characterization each coordinate ring is a finite type algebra over the corresponding base coordinate ring, so choose finitely many generators and, using the description of sections over a distinguished affine open, write each as a quotient of homogeneous sections of the section ring (proof lines 9441-9449).

Produce one immersion: take a common multiple N of all the degrees involved, form the sections obtained by multiplying the a_i and the products a_ij by suitable powers of a_i, observe that they lie in degrees N and generate the N-th power of the invertible sheaf, and obtain a morphism j to a projective space over S with the pullback of the twisting sheaf equal to that power (proof lines 9450-9466).

Check that j is an immersion: with coordinates named by the sections, the preimage of a standard affine open is the corresponding X_{a_i} and pulling back the quotients of coordinates recovers the chosen generators, so j restricts on each piece to a closed immersion into an affine open of projective space, whence j is an immersion (proof lines 9467-9478).

Upgrade from one power to all large powers: from the first part obtain an immersion given by sections of a fixed power; use ampleness to get a bound beyond which every power is globally generated; for a power above the sum of the two bounds choose additional sections generating the complementary power, form all products, and obtain a morphism i to projective space with the pullback of the twisting sheaf equal to that power (proof lines 9480-9505).

Check that i is an immersion: it factors as the product of j with the morphism given by the complementary sections followed by the Segre embedding; the product of an immersion with any morphism is an immersion by permanence, and a composite of immersions is an immersion, so i is an immersion (proof lines 9506-9515).
proof_roadmap: Cover X by finitely many ample distinguished affine opens mapping into affine charts of the base, and express generators of their coordinate rings through homogeneous sections (proof lines 9427-9449).

Bundle those sections into one large power to get an immersion into projective space (proof lines 9450-9478), then multiply the defining sections by generators of a complementary globally generated power to reach all large powers, checking immersiveness through the Segre embedding (proof lines 9480-9515).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a locally finite type morphism carrying an ample invertible sheaf there is a bound such that every larger power of the sheaf is the pullback of the twisting sheaf along an immersion into a projective space over the base (statement lines 9412-9425). The counted proof is a substantial construction: it uses ampleness to cover the source by finitely many distinguished affine opens over affine charts of the base, converts finite generators of the relevant coordinate rings into homogeneous sections of one common power, bundles them to build an immersion into projective space with the correct pullback of the twisting sheaf, and then upgrades the result from one power to all sufficiently large powers by multiplying with generators of a globally generated complementary power and checking immersiveness through the Segre embedding (proof lines 9427-9515). It is H2: every step of the construction is carried out inside the counted span, with the cited inputs being the standard ampleness, projective space and immersion statements.
